proposal.reactor_type: Stainless-steel/PFA coil reactor, thermally heated (oil bath or aluminum heating block) — thermal analog of microwave dielectric heating
proposal.tubing_material: PFA (perfluoroalkoxy) coil, chemically compatible with DMF and Pd catalysts at 50 °C; stainless steel acceptable alternative if higher pressure needed
proposal.residence_time_basis: reactor_volume_mL / total_flow_rate_mL_min (liquid-only system, no gas-phase compressibility correction)
proposal.light_setup: None — reaction is thermally driven (Pd-catalyzed Suzuki coupling); microwave dielectric heating is replaced by conductive/convective heating of the coil via a heated aluminum block or oil bath

streams.contents: Aromatic bromide (1.0 equiv) + Pd catalyst (e.g., Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(OAc)2/ligand, 2 mol%)
Phenylboronic acid derivative (1.2 equiv) + base (e.g., K2CO3 or Cs2CO3, 2.0 equiv)
streams.phase: liquid (fine suspension possible, filtered before pump)

proposal.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume PEEK T-mixer (500 µm internal channel) immediately upstream of heated coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Aryl halide and Pd catalyst are pre-mixed in one stream to allow oxidative addition to begin only upon contact with the boronic acid/base stream, preventing premature base-mediated protodeboronation or catalyst decomposition in a separate vessel. Combining at a T-mixer directly before the heated zone ensures reaction initiation coincides with thermal activation, mimicking the near-instantaneous heating of microwave irradiation.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas DMF (and DMF/H2O) with N2 sparge for 20 min to remove O2 and protect Pd(0) species
Dissolve/suspend K2CO3 or Cs2CO3 in DMF/H2O and filter through 0.2 µm inline filter to prevent clogging
Preheat both feed lines to 50 °C via preheating loops before the T-mixer to avoid cold-spot precipitation
Prime pumps and verify steady flow rates (0.5 mL/min each) before diverting to reactor
post_reactor_steps: In-line cooling loop (to ~25 °C) immediately after the reactor coil to quench the reaction and prevent further Pd-catalyzed side reactions
Back-pressure regulator set to 8 bar to maintain single-phase flow and suppress CO2 outgassing from carbonate base
Collect eluent into a stirred quench vessel; aqueous workup (extraction) performed off-line
Optional in-line UV/vis or FTIR monitoring to confirm conversion in real time
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling. Aryl bromide undergoes oxidative addition to Pd(0), followed by transmetalation with the arylboronate (formed in situ under basic conditions) and reductive elimination to give the biaryl product. Base (K2CO3/Cs2CO3) both activates the boronic acid and neutralizes HBr byproduct. Microwave heating in batch provided rapid, uniform superheating to 50 °C; in flow, this is replicated by a preheated, thermally conductive coil reactor to achieve equivalent residence time and thermal energy input. Degassing is critical to prevent Pd black formation and catalyst deactivation.

stage_1_mixing_reaction.description: T-mixing of Stream A and B followed by 10 min residence at 50 °C in a 10 mL coil

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Matches original 10 min microwave irradiation time; assumed transferable since both reflect exposure time at reaction temperature.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow of 1.0 mL/min (0.5 + 0.5 mL/min per stream) selected to give a practical reactor volume (10 mL) for a bench-top coil at the target 10 min residence time.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Directly matches batch microwave temperature (50 °C); no rate enhancement assumed from microwave-specific effects, per literature consensus that microwave heating in this context is purely thermal.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Assumed batch concentration ~0.4 M based on typical microwave vial loading (1.6 mmol in ~4 mL DMF, typical for small-scale MW Suzuki reactions). Each feed stream is prepared at 0.8 M so that 1:1 volumetric mixing dilutes it to final 0.4 M in the reactor, preserving equivalence to batch.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 8 bar chosen as a modest back pressure to prevent bubble formation from CO2 (carbonate decomposition) and to keep the reaction homogeneous below DMF's boiling point; not required for high-pressure superheating since 50 °C is well below DMF bp (153 °C).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Simple heated coil reactor chosen over microreactor chip due to potential particulate/base suspension; coil is more tolerant of solids and provides sufcient residence volume.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA selected for chemical inertness with DMF, Pd catalyst, and mild base slurries at 50 °C; also allows visual inspection for clogging.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 10 mL reactor volume matches the desired 10 min residence time at 1.0 mL/min combined flow.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Two-stream design separates the Pd/aryl halide from the boronic acid/base to control the onset of transmetalation and avoid pre-reactor side reactions.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume T-mixer minimizes back-mixing and ensures a well-defined onset of reaction time consistent with plug-flow assumption.

literature_analogies: Suzuki-Miyaura couplings performed in continuous flow using Pd homogeneous or immobilized catalysts in DMF/aqueous base mixtures at 50-100 °C, residence times 5-15 min (e.g., Org. Process Res. Dev. 2010, 14, 393; Noel & Buchwald flow Suzuki studies).

Direct microwave-to-flow translation approaches described by Kirschning and coworkers (Beilstein J. Org. Chem. 2011) equating microwave residence times to thermally heated coil reactor residence times.
Jensor/Jamison-type microreactor Suzuki couplings demonstrating feasibility of two-stream Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling in PFA/stainless steel coils under moderate back pressure.
safety_flags: Maintain inert (N2) atmosphere in feed reservoirs to prevent Pd(0) oxidation and catalyst deactivation
DMF thermal stability is not a concern at 50 °C, but avoid localized overheating from heating block hot-spots
Pd catalysts and boronic acids are potential respiratory/skin irritants — handle powders in fume hood before dissolution
Base (K2CO3/Cs2CO3) may generate CO2 gas in situ; ensure BPR and vented collection vessel to avoid pressure buildup
Verify no precipitation/clogging in feed lines, especially in the base-containing stream, using inline filters
Ensure electrical/heating safety for coil heater under continuous unattended operation (thermal cutoff recommended)
